scope: Refresh current LibreDWG and ACadSharp issue horizons
Classify reported failure routes separately across DWG, DXF, JSON, writer, projection, and native-consumer paths
Map relevant reports to existing local findings, implementation owners, and focused tests without duplicating work

method.kind: Primary repository issue-index/page research plus local plan/source/test-owner cross-check
localFilesInspected: DWG_DXF_OPEN_SOURCE_PARITY_PLAN.md: current issue mappings and PAR-14/19/22/26/33/52/126 owners
src/drw_entities.cpp: common DWG material/plotstyle flag and handle parsing
src/intern/dwgreader.cpp: block/compound entity traversal and publication paths
tests/gbk_codepage_tests.cpp: CP1254 Turkish-locale and CP949 end-to-end owners
method.limitations: LibreDWG issue pages #1450-#1452 and #1436/#1439 were not available beyond the current issue-index titles in this pass. No peer defect was reproduced locally. The ACadSharp #1282/#1283 full-body observations are carried forward from earlier plan research; this pass used the current index and did not acquire external samples.

evidence.observed: The index lists #1450 (R2007+ DXF LTYPE dash-text heap-buffer-overflow), #1451 (FIELD import with zero child values and use-after-free), #1452 (misaligned BITCODE_RS access in R2007+ XDATA/EED encoding), #1439 (LWPOLYLINE widths JSON-import overflow), and #1436 (R2007+ material-versus-plotstyle handle confusion). The issue titles do not establish matching libdxfrw defects, root causes, or current peer fix/release status.

Earlier full-body research in the plan records a DWG-writer extended-data per-APPID signed-size/cast and readback-loss report. Its reported threshold is peer-specific, not a format maximum or native-acceptance result.

Earlier full-body research in the plan records a nested-block deep-copy/stack-growth report in an Insert(BlockRecord) construction path. It does not establish recursive parsing behavior or illegal nesting in libdxfrw.

The report describes an AC1014 2D POLYLINE child VERTEX with AcDbVertex but no more-specific subtype marker, leaving a placeholder that later fails during typed builder construction. The issue is not a normative grammar statement.

The report describes current-culture lowercasing corrupting ANSI_1254 lookup under Turkish/Azeri cultures and therefore CP1254 text decoding. Local libdxfrw uses explicit ASCII folding and has a Turkish-locale generated CP1254 end-to-end control; this is not a literal .NET CultureInfo reproduction.

The report is an AC1032 DWG-writer/AutoCAD whole-file rejection for MTEXT frame-only flag 16, with 17 and an AC1027 control reported to open. The root cause is unresolved; matching entity bytes alone did not explain whole-file acceptance.

The report is a DWG-to-DXF conversion followed by GDAL spline projection failure. Its body does not provide machine-checkable offending spline arrays and independently measured expected geometry; linked artifacts were not downloaded.

The report compares DWG and AutoCAD-authored DXF TABLE block-cell value representations. Existing local PAR-126 work retains conservative incomplete-state behavior and generated ambiguity controls; the issue is not a general TABLE semantic oracle.

The project documents distinct fuzz/conversion entry points and route-specific class status. A reported or tested interface cannot be generalized to every format direction, entity class, build profile, and semantic outcome.
